title: Magna Carta sealed at Runnymede
summary: On 15 June 1215 King John sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede, a Thames meadow between Windsor and Staines, after rebel barons renounced their allegiance in May. The charter promised liberties to the English Church and free men and set up a council of 25 barons to enforce it. Pope Innocent III declared it void in August, civil war followed in September, and it was reissued in 1216, 1217 and 1225.

uncertainty.note: Dated 15 June 1215 in the charter and by both sources.

as_recorded.value: the fifteenth day of June in the seventeenth year of our reign
At Runnymede on June 15, King John accepted the terms that would become Magna Carta and placed his seal on the charter

where.historical_name: the meadow called Runnymede, between Windsor and Staines, in King John's kingdom of England

importance.justification: A charter binding the king to written terms, reissued repeatedly and later treated as a foundation of constitutional rights.

beats.caption: In May 1215 the barons and church representatives publicly withdraw their loyalty to King John, who then must negotiate.
At Runnymede on 15 June, John seals the charter, which binds the king and sets a council of 25 barons to enforce it.
Pope Innocent III declares the charter void in August and civil war breaks out in September, but reissues follow in 1216, 1217 and 1225.
